scenario.summary: The evidence leans negative. The plan is to keep exposure small or avoid it, and to name the level at which that view would be dropped.

more_positive_if: Growth scores only 6 of 100 against the comparison pool
Debt is as large as or larger than shareholders' equity (debt-to-equity 3.82)
The share price is 2.2% lower than a year ago
more_cautious_if: Profit grew 219% compared with a year earlier
Sales grew 47% compared with a year earlier
Over the past year the share did 0.6 percentage points better than the Nifty 50
notes: the ceiling is 10.0% of a portfolio: risk per position divided by the volatility-based stop distance, capped by your single-stock limit

prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on growth: profit grew 219% compared with a year earlier. Also in its favour: sales grew 47% compared with a year earlier; over the past year the share did 0.6 percentage points better than the Nifty 50; and at a 12% discount rate the price implies 3.0% yearly earnings growth for 10 years, a modest ask. Other areas on this side: the recent price trend, what the price implies.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on the recent price trend: the share price is 2.2% lower than a year ago. Also against it: the share price is 27% below its 52-week high; growth scores only 6 of 100 against the comparison pool; and debt is as large as or larger than shareholders' equity (debt-to-equity 3.82). Other areas on this side: growth, the balance sheet, cash flow and the balance sheet.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 4 points in favour and 6 against give more points against. The pool score is 43 of 100. The side that carries most weight is the recent price trend. That gives an educational rating of Underweight with high confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
